messages.author: d2bffd1a5d780ca8
messages.subject: Error message in measEq.syntax
parts:
Dear Professor Terrence,

I’m glad to greet you again.

I’m experiencing some troubles when using the measEq.syntax function, in fact, I have already experienced this problem in the past. I attached the script and the data in order to allow you to verify directly.

When I run the compareFit argument (comparing all models at once) I get this error message: “Error in svd(X): a dimension is zero”. Nevertheless, when I try to compare two models at a time, the code works fine until the comparison of strict and scalar models is set, which makes me think that the problem is caused by something in these models.

I really would appreciate your help with this issue. Thanks in advance.

Best regards.

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Error message in measEq.syntax
parts: I’m experiencing some troubles when using the measEq.syntax function, in fact, I have already experienced this problem in the past. I attached the script and the data in order to allow you to verify directly.

Did we not solve it before?  I took me a while to realize (again?) you choose parameterization="theta" to generate your syntax, but not when you fit the model (using the default parameterization="delta").  Fix that and it runs fine (and I'm guessing the warnings disappear when you fit your first 4 models)

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Error message in measEq.syntax
parts: Is it essential to specify the argument parameterization = "theta" when my interest is only to fit my ordered data (not to evaluate measurement invariance)?

that argument is only relevant when your data are ordered.  If you are not interested in testing strict invariance, it is not important whether you use delta or theta parameterization (statistically equivalent), even if you are testing equivalent of thresholds, loadings, and intercepts.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Professor,

I have a simple question about which estimator do you recommend. I have a pretty small sample (n = 200) and I need to run a CFA for a three factor model with 42 indicators (items). The scale is designed in Likert format with five answer options (e.g. 1, 2, 3, 4, 5).

Should I use MLM or MLR due to sample size and assume the data as continuous? Or should I choose WLSMV and ignore the possible effect of sample size?

Thanks again. Best regards.

Have a nice day.
